content_record.title: Mitochondrial superoxide: a developmental signal that preserves nuclear envelope integrity
content_record.editorial_body: A new study reveals that a burst of mitochondrial superoxide during development programs long-term nuclear envelope health by curbing unsaturated fat synthesis and lipid peroxidation. Reduced ETC activity preserves nuclear envelope morphology in aging worms. Developmental superoxide downregulates SBP-1, lowering unsaturated fatty acids. Lipid peroxidation control extends lifespan and eases progeria phenotypes. This signal is based on Mitochondrial superoxide regulates nuclear envelope integrity and ageing via redox-mediated lipid metabolism. from PubMed. Read the original report for full context.
